items.q: they finally ended up selecting Arthur Gibbs... Now, we rehearsed this show; we tried out in Detroit; we played Philadelphia

ctx.x: Billy was...oh, he was some showman. 'Course, wait 'til I tell you what Tallulah Bankhead did to him. He wanted untrained sound. He wanted it to be primitive,

and this is what I was playing. But he wanted that other piano player to be able to play with me, which would show a contrast, yet it would be similar, or it could work together. So here we come...we tried everybody...James P.--I thought James P. was going to get it. And Willie 'the Lion,' I thought he was going to get it...I thought they was going to go by the name of a person, you know, but they finally ended up selecting Arthur Gibbs, the man that wrote "Running Wild."

Now, we rehearsed this show; we tried out in Detroit; we played Philadelphia; and one day in New York when we were getting ready to open, Tallulah Bankhead went up on the right side of the theater and there was a scene where that you could not see her, you know, for that's like a fleeting moment. She would disappear from view. And she said to Billy, and God for me to give me if they don't want tell what happened. She said to Billy, "Billy, I'm lost."
